title: Agile-DRAM: Agile Trade-Offs in Memory Capacity, Latency, and Energy for Data Centers
problem: Data centers experience significant memory under-utilization due to infrastructure overprovisioning, inefficient workload scheduling, and limited server configurations. This under-utilization results in wasted capacity and suboptimal energy efficiency.
motivation: Dynamically converting idle memory capacity into reduced latency and power consumption can improve data center efficiency and performance without requiring additional hardware investment.
method: Agile-DRAM modifies conventional DRAM architecture with minor changes to support three operational modes: low-latency, low-power, and max-capacity. The system enables runtime switching between modes in response to workload fluctuations, converting under-utilized memory capacity into either reduced access latency or reduced power consumption depending on data center needs.
key_novelty: A DRAM architecture that dynamically trades off memory capacity for latency and power efficiency through multiple runtime-reconfigurable operational modes.
contributions: Agile-DRAM architecture supporting three operational modes with runtime mode switching
Hardware mechanism for converting under-utilized capacity into latency or power benefits
25.8% single-core speedup and 22.4% energy reduction in low-latency mode
31.6% standby power and 85.7% self-refresh power reduction in low-power mode
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Dynamic memory capacity-latency-power tradeoffs for data centers
